newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopians urged to back action against Somalia.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopians urged to back action against Somalia.

text.p: A state-owned newspaper on Thursday urged support for the Ethiopian army in launching attacks into neighbouring Somalia against what it said were extremist Moslem fundamentalists.
The Amharic-language daily Addis Zemen said the "terrorist band" of extremists had tried to attack the border town of Dollo from Somalia.

"The action taken by the defence forces to crush the terrorist group was praiseworthy. It shows to all those who may have similar designs to violate the country's sovereignty that they would be dealt with without mercy," the paper said.
It called on the Ethiopian people to remain vigilant and support the defence forces in their struggle against extremist Moslems bent on imposing fundamentalism by force.
Ethiopia, in its first comment on the border situation, said on Wednesday that its defence forces killed or wounded more than 100 Moslem fundamentalists who had tried to attack Dollo.
The statement said those killed included Arabs from a number of countries. It gave no indication of Ethiopian casualties and did not say how far Ethiopian forces had penetrated into Somalia.
Reports from Mogadishu, the Somali capital, earlier alleged that Ethiopian forces had invaded western Somalia and captured several towns there.
It was the second time in four months that Ethiopian forces had crossed into Somalia to attack what Ethiopia said were hostile Moslem fundamentalist groups there.
Last August Ethiopia said its forces killed more than 230 fighters of the al-Ittihad Moslem group and destroyed three of their camps in eastern Somalia.
